results.reason: Part 1 says the 10-Business-Day §5.7(b) window for the September 14 First Schedule Supplement expired. It cites the October 13 Second Supplement letter. It explains that under §5.7(c) Ferrovane is deemed cured for Article IX and §7.2(a), so Buyer has lost both its walk right and its indemnity.

Part 3 says Escrow Agreement §1.1 limits Losses to actual out-of-pocket amounts and excludes diminution in value, lost profits and attorneys' fees. It explains that §4.3 combined with SPA §11.11 makes the narrower definition control escrow recovery.

Part 2 says MSA §14.2 treats acquiring more than 50% of voting equity as an assignment needing Tavinor's consent, and that the 100% share sale triggers it. It notes the consent is missing from Annex 7.2(d), §5.3 and §7.2(d), and that §4.4 is inaccurate. It concludes Buyer could be forced to close and then face termination or repricing by its sole-source supplier.
The memo says the window closed on Monday, September 28, 2026, more than two weeks before the October 13 letter.
The memo states the indemnity escrow is $4,850,000.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has 'Where it appears', 'Why it matters for Harrowgate' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Part 6 is an open-points table listing unresolved items and who needs to supply each one, including the client.
The memo states expressly that Harrowgate no longer has a termination right for Ferrovane. The live window it discusses relates only to the Second Supplement.
The memo states that Tavinor's consent is not listed in Annex 7.2(d) and is not a closing condition.
